senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. תָּקַל) [to bring into contact, knock, insert,]
to drive a peg in, put up a tent; to fasten.
units: <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 981:1">Yalk. Cant. 981</cite> <he>הלואי יִתְקַע תורתי בלבנו וכ׳</he> Oh that he would drive his law into our heart as in former days.

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 1">Ex. R. s. 1<sup>17</sup></cite> Caleb is named Tekoa (<cite ref="I Chronicles 2:24">I Chr. II, 24</cite>), <he>שת׳ לבו לאביו וכ׳</he> because he fastened his heart on his father in heaven.

Yeb. 109ᵇ תּוֹקֵעַ עצמו לדבר הלכה he who nails himself to the matter of the law, i.e. confines himself to study, and is remiss in practical conduct; ואיבעית אימא תוקע … בדיינא וכ׳ or I may explain, ‘he who nails himself to the matter of the law’ refers to a judge before whom a case comes, and he having learned a certain hălakhah decides by analogy, while there is a greater scholar than he whom he fails to consult; a. e.—Part. pass. תָּקוּעַ lodged, placed.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 85b:8">B. Mets. 85ᵇ</cite> <he>אצל מי אתה ת׳</he> next to whom art thou placed (in heaven)? <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 9:2:3">Y. Sot. IX, 23ᶜ</cite> <he>והסכין ת׳ בלבו</he> with the knife sticking in his heart; a. e.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 18b:17">B. Kam. 18ᵇ</cite> <he>תרנגול … ות׳ בו ושברו</he> if a cock put his head into a glass vessel and crowed into it, and broke it; <cite ref="Kiddushin 24b:11">Kidd. 24ᵇ</cite>.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 24b:11">Ib.</cite> <he>ת׳ באזנו וכ׳</he> if one blew on a horn into a person’s ear, and made him deaf; a. e.—Esp.
<cite ref="Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 3:5">R. Hash. III, 5</cite> <he>בר״ה תּוֹקְעִין בשל זכרים</he> on New Year’s day they blow on a ram’s horn.
<cite ref="Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 3:7">Ib. 7</cite> <he>התוקע לתוך הבור וכ׳</he> if one blows (the Shofar) into a pit &c.

<cite ref="Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 4:1">Ib. IV, 1</cite> <he>יום טוב … תוקעים וכ׳</he> when New Year fell on a Sabbath, they blew in the Temple, but not in the country. Ib. 8 <he>אין מעכבין … מלִתְקוֹעַ</he> we do not prevent children from blowing the Shofar (on the Sabbath). Ib. 9 <he>תוקע ומריע ותוקע</he>, v. <cite ref="T00415"><he>רוּעַ</he> I</cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Taanit 2:5">Taan. II, 5</cite> <he>תִּקְעיּ הכהנים תָּקְעוּ וכ׳</he> (the reader said,) sound the T’ḳiʿah, you priests, and they did so, (upon which he said,) He who has answered &c.; a. v. fr.—[

senses.gloss: to slap with the back of the hand.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 8:6">B. Kam. VIII, 6</cite> (<cite ref="Bava Kamma 90a:13">90ᵃ</cite>) <he>התוקע לחבירו</he> he who slaps his neighbor on the ear; oth. opin. who shouts into his neighbor’s ear.]
<cite ref="Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 4:7">R. Hash. IV, 7</cite> <he>השני מַתְקִיעַ</he> the second reader orders the blowing of the Shofar.
<cite ref="Yevamot 54a">Yeb. 54ᵃ</cite> <he>ונ׳</he> and his membrum was inserted.
<cite ref="Taanit 24a:10">Taan. 24ᵃ</cite> <he>אוי לו לדור שנ׳ בכך</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>שכן נ׳</he>) woe to the generation that is placed in such a (bad) position.
